identity.title: A Disk-based Dynamical Mass Estimate for the Young Binary AK Sco

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present spatially and spectrally resolved Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of gas and dust in the disk orbiting the pre-main sequence binary AK Sco.

question.value: What is the dynamical mass of the AK Sco binary from its circumbinary disk CO rotation curve, and how does it compare with RV constraints and pre-MS evolutionary model predictions?

evidence.quote: Here we report the direct determination of the AK Sco binary mass through the dynamical measurement of its circumbinary disk rotation profile using new data from ALMA.

analysis_steps.goal: Forward-model CO visibilities with disk model

method.value: Parametric disk structure with LTE RADMC-3D ray tracing at 2.5 AU pixels, FFT and interpolation onto observed uv points, chi^2 likelihood

evidence.quote: We then employed the `FFTW` algorithm (cite: fftw) to Fourier transform these spectral images, and then performed a band-limited interpolation of the complex visibilities onto the same spatial frequencies

key_parameters.value: 12 free parameters: T10, q, Mco, rc, xi, M*, i_d, phi, offsets, vsys, d; gamma fixed to 1

evidence.quote: The gradient parameter $\gamma$ is fixed to unity

assumptions.value: LTE level populations; Keplerian rotation dominated by binary mass; vertical hydrostatic equilibrium; vertically isothermal

evidence.quote: The bulk velocity field of the gas is assumed to be Keplerian, and dominated by the binary mass

fitting.value: MCMC with Metropolis-Hastings; uniform priors except Gaussian prior on d (142+/-6 pc); tuned jump covariance; multiple chains, Gelman-Rubin convergence

evidence.quote: we employed the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) technique with a Metropolis-Hastings (M-H) jump proposal.

validation.value: reduced chi^2 = 1.08, image-plane residual comparison, trial fit at 122 kHz recovers same values

evidence.quote: The reduced $\chi^2$ of the best-fit model is 1.08.

method.value: Convert RV M sin^3 i using disk inclination assuming co-planarity; derive dynamical distance from M/d and M sin^3 i

findings_qualitative.value: Disk is compact (rc ~14 AU) with ~5-10 MJup of gas and dust, detected in continuum, CO, 13CO and C18O

evidence.quote: A relatively compact disk in orbit around the AK Sco binary, with $\sim$5–10 $M_{\rm Jup}$ of gas and dust

findings_qualitative.value: Eccentric disk ruled out: e_d < 0.04 at 99.7% confidence

evidence.quote: with $e_d < 0.04$ (at 99.7% confidence)

claims.hypothesis: Can a disk rotation-curve fit give an accurate binary mass?
claims.experiment: Forward model CO 2-1 visibilities with RADMC-3D and MCMC
claims.result: M* = 2.49+/-0.10 Msun, consistent with RV-derived 2.52+/-0.03 Msun if coplanar
claims.finding: Disk-based dynamical mass method is validated

evidence.quote: This consistency between mass constraints, along with the similar results for the V4046 Sgr binary (cite: rosenfeld12), effectively validates the absolute accuracy of the disk-based dynamical mass measurement technique.

claims.hypothesis: Do pre-MS evolutionary models reproduce the dynamical mass?
claims.experiment: SED fit and mapping onto four model grids
claims.result: Models give 2.60-2.71 Msun, 1.5-2 sigma above dynamical mass, age 18+/-1 Myr
claims.finding: Models are marginally consistent but systematically high by 7-10%

evidence.quote: These model-predicted masses are consistent, but are all $\sim$1.5–2 $\sigma$ higher than the dynamical mass inferred from the ALMA data.

claims.hypothesis: Is the ALMA mass consistent with the interferometric/astrometric mass of Anthonioz et al.?
claims.result: Their M*=2.80+/-0.11 Msun is a 2 sigma discrepancy
claims.finding: Minor tension, possibly from warp or ring model simplicity

evidence.quote: a 2 $\sigma$ discrepancy with respect to the disk-based mass estimate
